content.text:
The tool reported an average of 3,000 steps per day for October 1–3, 2026. That figure looks questionable, because the summary contradicts itself.

| Date | Steps | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Oct 1 | none | No record, so treated as missing |
| Oct 2 | 0 | Counted as a data day, but also appears to be flagged as no-wear |
| Oct 3 | 6,000 | Valid |

**The 3,000 figure:** it is (0 + 6,000) ÷ 2. That counts Oct 2's zero as a real day.

**The inconsistency:** the same summary says one no-wear day was excluded. Fitbit days with 0 steps and a full day of sedentary time are treated as no-wear. Oct 2 is the only zero-step day, so it is probably the excluded one. If it is, the average is **6,000 steps**, based on Oct 3 alone. The summary still counts Oct 2 in its "2 days with data" and in the mean, so I can't tell which figure it actually used. I could pull the raw Oct 2 record to settle it, if you want.

**How missing and no-wear days affect an average:**
- **Missing days (Oct 1):** these are left out, not counted as zero. Counting them as zero would pull the average down without any evidence you were inactive.
- **No-wear days (probably Oct 2):** a 0 usually means the tracker wasn't worn or didn't sync, not that you took no steps. Including it drags the average down, here from 6,000 to 3,000.
- **Coverage:** only 1–2 of the 3 days have usable data (66.7% coverage if Oct 2 is counted, 33% if not). Either average rests on very little data. A single day also can't support a trend.

If you didn't wear your tracker on Oct 1–2, 6,000 is the better estimate of your activity. It only reflects Oct 3, though.
